steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Beat butter or margarine and brown and white sugars together until creamy. Add eggs and vanilla; beat well. Combine flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt in a separate bowl; add to butter-sugar mixture, stirring until well combined. Stir in oats and raisins; mix well.

Drop dough by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets. Bake until cookies are almost set, 10 to 12 minutes. Do not overbake. Cool 1 minute on cookie sheets, then move to wire racks. Cool; store tightly covered.

raw_recipe.headline: Cocoa Oatmeal Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These delicious cocoa oatmeal cookies are made with cocoa and have raisins added for a chocolate version of this classic and tasty cookie style.
raw_recipe.name: Cocoa Oatmeal Cookies

review.reviewBody: While I did make a couple of changes, I'm sure that as is, these cookies are wonderful. First, I changed the recipe to make 24 cookies. Then I added about 2 T of softened/melted peanut butter as the last ingredient while omitting the raisins. I thought the batter was to die for, but then I tried a cookie. It was fluffy and moist on the inside. Perfect in my book! They remind me of my childhood fav- no bake cookies. So I guess these are Bake, No-bake cookies.

I added about 1 cup of chopped almonds, about 1 1/2 tsp cinnamon, dried blueberries, dried cherries, and raisins to make about 1 cup (instead of just raisins), and substituted half of the butter with applesauce. Baked for about 13-14 minutes, the cookies came out slightly cakey, moist, hearty, and DELICIOUS!

Really good! I subbed 1/2 cup peanut butter chips and 1/2 cup chocolate chips for the raisins, as the folks I'm making these for aren't fans of raisins in cookies. I might try adding a bit more cocoa powder next time, but still these are very good. If you overbake, they will dry out a bit - 12 minutes was perfect for heaping tablespoonfuls of dough.

These are great, and perfect to make with my 5-year old helper! We subbed half chocolate and half white chocolate chips for the raisins, and thet turned out fudgy and just right.

We rolled them into balls for uniformity, and they spread perfectly, 11.5 minutes bake time.

heavenly, added 4 heaping tablespoons peanut butter and didn't make any additions (no raisins, chips, etc) . wonderful recipe, smells delish baking. i baked mine at 350 for exactly 10 minutes on parchment and they are the wonderful combo between a crisp outside and lovely soft interior. the batter was quite soft (although my house is quite warm today) so i refridgerated 10 mins before and kept batter in fridge while they baked. didn't spread at all. YUM!

These were fantastic, because they're easy to make and it's very easy to eat one at a time. They're pretty filling, and the calorie count isn't too obscene. What I did was I split the batter into two after adding the dry ingredients, and only added the cocoa to one half....the other half I added about 1/3 c of crunchy peanut butter and a little cinnamon, and they turned out terrific! Amazing. I added some chocolate chips to the chocolate ones, and they were very chocolately. A little powdered sugar on top and they were good to go! I also needed to add a little bit more oats to both, for a heavier consistency. So overall this is an outstanding recipe to add on to and play with.

I made these with my kids and they were fabulous!!! I couldn't stop eating them. I used 1 cup chocolate chips instead of raisins as we are big chocolate fans and raisins not so much. I also used quick oats instead of rolled. I did make the cookies a little larger and left the cooking temp and time the same to compensate for the quick oats. They turned out with the perfect feel and texture outside and the perfect gooey-ness inside

I changed the recipe to fit my health standards. Instead of the butter I used 1/2 cup coconut oil and 3 small grated, peeled apples. When I was done the dough/batter looked too wet, so I added almost a whole cup of flour! I think next time I will put in a lot less flour, but they did end up as very interesting lump-shaped cookies. They have a kind of mild chocolate flavor - I'll add more cocoa next time, but overall this is a really great cookie!

I made these GLUTEN FREE by substituting rice flour for ap. flour and used McCann's quick oats. Also used 1c. GF. choc. chips. don't make too big and bake for 12 min. If too big, they become lacy. Nice cookie! No one will know the difference.

Quick, easy and tasty child-friendly recipe. Easy to follow with minimal mess/cleanup. Only modifications I made was to substitute the raisins for semi-sweet chocolate chips and to add an upside-down bittersweet chocolate hershey's kiss to the centre. (The chocolate in the centre was esthetically pleasing and added a nice surprise when you bit into them). I made the cookies slightly larger and increased the cooking time slightly to 13 minutes. Ended up nicely moist in the centre with a slight crunch to the outside. Found them a bit sweet (even the bites without chocolate), so next time I would cut back the sugar. All around a yummy cookie.

These cookies came out really good. I made a huge mistake by putting the dough on parchment paper, then they started to burn in the oven...oops. Then realized to put them on regular baking sheets- what a difference. I made a couple of revisions: I substituted regular flour for whole wheat flour, and since I didn't have any cocoa powder, I used instant coffee instead. I omitted the raisins too. Delicious! Nice and moist.
I love this. I get the health benefit of oats and the taste of chocolate.

This recipe was fab. Great texture, raisins add the moisture. I reduced the sugar taking out white sugar, using 2tbsp icing sugar instead. I topped a few of the warm cookies with a tablespoon of nutella 😛
What is there not to like? Everything is perfect. I added walnuts into mine. Yum!
I made them GF. Added chocolate chips and dried cherries.

I had no idea what to expect by these but they are DELISH! Who knew a cross between a brownie and an oatmeal raisin cookie would be so good? They might even be good with some chocolate chips added. Definitely follow the instructions to make sure they aren’t overly set when you pull them, as they end up so soft when made as written!
Awesome cookie! I used special dark cocoa, that's why they are darker. My hubby taste tested and he said "don't take them to the outing, I like those!" You are right, do not overbake!

The only of change I made was shortening instead of butter. That's just the way I make cookies and I prefer the texture. I guess I also made them a little bigger than described. Baked for 10 minutes. These are easy and good. Not too sweet. Hit with my crew. Will surely make again.
Excellent cookie. The only thing I changed was using 1/2 cup raisins and 1/2 cup of dried cranberries.
I made 24- halved all quantities as per the automatic calculations. Amazing.
